sections.heading: What a good resignation letter contains
sections.body:
A short letter does the job. It usually includes these parts:

- The date you are leaving, stated in the first paragraph.
- A plain sentence that you are resigning.
- A short thank you for the chance to work there.
- An offer to help with the handover.
- Your contact details, if your employer may need them after you leave.

Keep any reason short, or leave it out. You do not owe a long explanation, and complaints do not belong in a letter you may need to show later.

**Check every fact in the draft before you send it.** The date, the company name and your job title are the details people notice first.

pages.h1: How to write a good resignation letter
pages.claim: A good resignation letter says you are leaving, gives your last working day, thanks your employer and offers help with the handover. Keep it short and neutral. Use the free generator to draft yours in a tone you pick.

sections.heading: The parts of a good resignation letter
sections.body:
A good letter is short. Most have four parts, in this order.

1. **Opening:** say that you are resigning and give your last working day.
2. **Thanks:** name one real thing you gained from the job, such as a skill or some experience.
3. **Handover:** offer to finish open work or train the person who takes over.
4. **Close:** sign off with your name and contact details.

Three short paragraphs are enough. A reader should get the key facts from the first two lines.

sections.heading: A sample you can adapt
sections.body:
Replace the text in brackets with your own details. Keep the sentences you like and change the rest.

Dear [Manager's name],

Please accept this letter as notice of my resignation from my position as [role] at [company]. My last working day will be [date].

Thank you for the chance to work on [a project or area you are proud of]. I learned a lot here, especially about [skill].

Before I leave, I am glad to finish [open task] and help [name] with the handover. Please tell me what would help most.

Thank you again. [Your name], [email], [phone]

sections.heading: What to leave out
sections.body:
Leave out complaints, criticism of managers or coworkers, and personal details about health or family. A resignation letter may be kept on file, so write only what you would say to the person in a meeting.

You do not need to give a reason. If you choose to give one, keep it to one short sentence.

sections.heading: Use the generator for a first draft
sections.body:
The [resignation letter generator](https://resignation-letter.lazur.app/) writes a draft from your role, company and last working day. Pick the tone that fits your relationship with your manager: warm and grateful, short and formal, or neutral. Add a note for anything you want included, such as a handover task.

Read the draft against the four parts above. Check the date, the company name and the role first, since a wrong detail is the easiest mistake to miss. Then change any sentence that does not sound like you.

sections.heading: Email or in person?
sections.body:
Check how your company handles resignations. Some ask for a written letter to HR or your manager. Others want a conversation first, then a letter. If you talk first, keep the letter short and send it after the conversation, so the two match.

Your contract or employee handbook usually sets the notice period, so look there before you pick your last day.

If you are leaving a team you are close to, you can say so in one line near the end, such as that you will miss working with them. Keep that line warm and brief, and leave out any detail about what went wrong. Once the letter is ready, read it through one last time and confirm that the date and the company name are exactly right.

faq.q: What should a good resignation letter say?
faq.a: It should say you are resigning, give your last working day, thank your employer and offer help with the handover. Keep it short, neutral and free of complaints. Three short paragraphs is enough for most letters.

faq.q: What not to say when resigning?
faq.a: Avoid complaints, criticism of people and personal details. Do not explain problems in the letter. If you want to raise a concern, do it in a separate meeting. Keep every sentence something you would say to your manager's face.

faq.q: Should I explain why I am resigning?
faq.a: You do not have to. A short reason, such as a move or a new field, is enough if you want to give one. Leave it out if the reason is complicated or personal. Your last day is the part the letter must get right.
